description_full: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners PLC, together with its subsidiaries, produces, distributes, and sells a range of non-alcoholic ready-to-drink beverages. It offers flavours, mixers, energy drinks, soft drinks, water, enhanced water, isotonic drinks, tea and coffee, juices, and other drinks. The company provides its products under the Coca-Cola Original Taste, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, Diet Coke, Sprite, Sprite Zero Sugar, Fanta, Fanta Zero Sugar, Monster Energy, A&W, Absolut Vodka & SPRITE, Ades, Appletiser, aquaBona, Aquarius, BACARDÍ Mixed with Coca Cola RTD, Barista Bros, Bonaqua, BURN, Deep Spring, Dr Pepper, Dr Pepper Zero Sugar, Feral Brewing Co, Fuze Tea, Giancarlo Coffee, GLACEAU smartwater, Grinders, HALO, Jack Daniel's & Coca-Cola ready-to-drink, Kristal, L&P, MER, Minute Maid, Mother, Mount Franklin, Nordic Mist, Nutriboost, Oasis, Pulpy, pump, pumped, Reign, Rekorderlig Cider, Relentless, Royal, Royal Bliss, Schweppes, Schweppes Mix, SOCO, URGE, Vilas del Turbón, Voyage, Wilkins Pure, and Zephyr Coffee Co brands. It is also involved in the bottling and other operations. The company was formerly known as Coca-Cola European Partners plc and changed its name to Coca-Cola Europacific Partners PLC in May 2021. The company was founded in 1904 and is based in Uxbridge, United Kingdom.

financial_summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners  is a large-cap consumer defensive business with a $51.0B market cap on $23.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 7% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $2.5B in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.49× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 9.1×.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 56% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 6pp above the Consumer Defensive median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.66x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.7% of sector revenue and 1.2% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+23.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.07 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 38% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 18% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 2% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 24% and a beta of 0.57, it is more defensive than the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $169.6M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 48% in the 2020 crash, 28% in the 2022 bear market and 71% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $110 (margin of safety -6%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 21%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $77.71 to $162 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Defensive peers: EV/EBITDA 17.7 vs 10.3 and P/FCF 20.8 vs 16.0 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 53% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 12 covering analysts target $112 on average, 3% below the price.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 6.9%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.27).
It runs a 37% gross margin and converts 11% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.49x.
ROE of 25% is amplified by 3.8x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.3x net debt to EBITDA ($1.0B of cash against $11.4B of debt), with interest covered 9.1x.
The current ratio of 0.80 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.0% over 3 years and 14.3% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
Free cash flow has compounded 13.8% a year over five years.
Analysts expect 9.7% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 56.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 38%.
It returns 2.1% a year to shareholders (0.1% in buybacks and 2.1% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 39 consecutive years, raising it 18.9% a year over the last five.
people: With about 37,003 employees, each generates about $629K of revenue, 1.2x the Consumer Defensive median, and productivity has risen 8.3% a year.
That works out to $66K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $4.7M (8x revenue per employee).
